Minimizer module

GUMP GPD global fit: cost function and iMinuit-based fitting interface.

Loads and preprocesses all experimental datasets (PDFs, tPDFs, GFFs, GPDs, DVCS cross-sections and asymmetries, DVMP cross-sections for rho, phi, and J/psi), builds NLO theory predictions via gumpgpd.Observables, gumpgpd.DVCS_xsec, and gumpgpd.DVMP_xsec, and exposes a single iMinuit-based fit driver: off_forward_fit_withH_withHt().

gumpgpd.Minimizer.CFF_theo(xB, t, Q, Para_Unp, Para_Pol, porder=2)[source]

Compute the four Compton form factors (CFFs) at a given kinematic point.

The skewness is derived from \(x_B\), \(t\), and \(Q\) via the exact kinematic relation.

Parameters:

  • xB (float) – Bjorken-\(x\) variable.

  • t (float) – Momentum transfer squared \(t\).

  • Q (float) – Photon virtuality \(Q\).

  • Para_Unp (np.ndarray) – Unpolarized GPD parameter array (species-stacked).

  • Para_Pol (np.ndarray) – Polarized GPD parameter array (species-stacked).

  • porder (int, optional) – Perturbative order. Defaults to 2 (NLO).

Returns:

[HCFF, ECFF, HtCFF, EtCFF] — the four CFFs as scalars (or arrays if the input parameters have a batch dimension).

Return type:

list

Return type:

gumpgpd.Minimizer.DVMP_L_Error_Prop(DVMP_tot_xsec: DataFrame, meson: int = 1)[source]

Error propagation for dσ_L /dt= (dσ_tot /dt) / (ε(y) + 1/R(Q;a,p,meson)).

Parameters:

  • DVMP_tot_xsec (DataFrame) – total cross-sections including at least four column: ‘y’, ‘Q’, ‘f’ and ‘delta f’ for lepton energy loss, photon virtuality, total cross-sections and uncertainties of total cross-sections.

  • meson – 1 for rho production

Returns:

dσ_L(y,Q,a,p,meson) / dt with standart deviation

gumpgpd.Minimizer.DVMPxsec_theo(DVMPxsec_data: DataFrame, Para_Unp, xsec_norm, meson: int, p_order=2)[source]

Compute DVMP cross-section predictions for a full dataset using a parallel pool.

Parameters:

  • DVMPxsec_data (pd.DataFrame) – Full DVMP cross-section dataset.

  • Para_Unp (np.ndarray) – Unpolarized parameter array.

  • xsec_norm (float) – Overall normalization applied as theory *= xsec_norm**2.

  • meson (int) – Meson type: 1 for \(\rho^0\), 3 for J/psi.

  • p_order (int, optional) – Perturbative order. Defaults to 2.

Returns:

Concatenated results with 'pred f' and 'cost' columns.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

gumpgpd.Minimizer.Export_Frame_Append(df, filename, export_path=None)[source]

Append (or create) a CSV file inside <export_path>/GUMP_Results/.

On the first call for a given filename the file is created and the header row is written. Subsequent calls append rows without repeating the header.

Parameters:

  • df (pd.DataFrame) – Data to write.

  • filename (str) – Name of the CSV file (e.g. 'PDFcomp.csv').

  • export_path (str, optional) – Root directory for output. Defaults to the module-level SAVE_TO_FILE_PATH.

gumpgpd.Minimizer.GFF_theo(GFF_input: DataFrame, Para: array, p_order=2, chunksize=None)[source]

Compute NLO GFF theory predictions for an entire dataset in parallel.

Adds a 'pred f' column with the theory prediction and, if 'f' and 'delta f' columns are present, a 'cost' column with the per-point \(\chi^2\) contribution.

Parameters:

  • GFF_input (pd.DataFrame) – Input data with columns j, t, Q, flv, spe, and optionally f/delta f.

  • Para (np.ndarray) – Full stacked parameter array indexed by species.

  • p_order (int, optional) – Perturbative order. Defaults to 2 (NLO).

  • chunksize (int, optional) – Pool map chunksize for performance tuning.

Returns:

Copy of GFF_input with added 'pred f' and (if data present) 'cost' columns.

Return type:

pd.DataFrame

gumpgpd.Minimizer.GFF_theo_scalar_helper(j_i, x, xi, t_i, Q_i, p_i, flv_i, Para_i, p_order)[source]

Compute a single GFF theory value for use with multiprocessing.Pool.starmap().

Parameters:

  • j_i (int) – Mellin moment index \(j\).

  • x (float) – Momentum fraction (set to 0 for GFFs).

  • xi (float) – Skewness (set to 0 for GFFs).

  • t_i (float) – Momentum transfer squared \(t\).

  • Q_i (float) – Factorization/evolution scale \(Q\).

  • p_i (int) – 1 for vector GPDs (H, E), -1 for axial-vector GPDs (Ht, Et).

  • flv_i (str) – Flavor label.

  • Para_i (np.ndarray) – Parameter array for this kinematic point.

  • p_order (int) – Perturbative order (1 = LO, 2 = NLO).

Returns:

Theory prediction for the \(j=0\) GFF moment.

Return type:

float

Compute a single GPD theory value for use with multiprocessing.Pool.starmap().

gumpgpd.Minimizer.TFF_theo(xB, t, Q, Para_Unp, meson: int, p_order=2, muset=1, flv='All')[source]

Compute the two transition form factors (TFFs) for DVMP at a given kinematic point.

The skewness is derived from \(x_B\), \(t\), and \(Q\). For J/psi production the J/psi mass enters the skewness formula.

Parameters:

  • xB (float) – Bjorken-\(x\) variable.

  • t (float) – Momentum transfer squared \(t\).

  • Q (float) – Photon virtuality \(Q\).

  • Para_Unp (np.ndarray) – Unpolarized GPD parameter array (species-stacked).

  • meson (int) – Meson type: 1 for \(\\rho^0\), 2 for \(\\phi\), 3 for J/psi.

  • p_order (int, optional) – Perturbative order. Defaults to 2 (NLO).

  • muset (float, optional) – Scale factor applied to \(Q\) when evaluating the TFF (used for scale-uncertainty studies).

  • flv (str, optional) – Flavor channel. Defaults to 'All'.

Returns:

[HTFF, ETFF] — the H- and E-type TFFs.

Return type:

list

gumpgpd.Minimizer.cost_off_forward_withH_withHt(Norm_HuV, alpha_HuV, beta_HuV, alphap_HuV, Invm2_HuV, Norm_Hubar, alpha_Hubar, beta_Hubar, alphap_Hqbar, Norm_Hubar_2, alpha_Hubar_2, beta_Hubar_2, Norm_HdV, alpha_HdV, beta_HdV, alphap_HdV, Invm2_HdV, Norm_Hdbar, alpha_Hdbar, beta_Hdbar, Norm_Hdbar_2, alpha_Hdbar_2, beta_Hdbar_2, Norm_Hg, alpha_Hg, beta_Hg, alphap_Hg, Invm2_Hg, Norm_Hg_2, alpha_Hg_2, beta_Hg_2, Norm_EuV, alpha_EuV, beta_EuV, alphap_EuV, Norm_EdV, alpha_EdV, beta_EdV, alphap_EdV, R_E_ubar, R_E_dbar, R_E_g, R_Hu_xi2, R_Hd_xi2, R_Hg_xi2, R_Eu_xi2, R_Ed_xi2, R_Eg_xi2, R_Hu_xi4, R_Hd_xi4, R_Hg_xi4, R_Eu_xi4, R_Ed_xi4, R_Eg_xi4, bexp_HSea, bexp_Hg, Norm_HtuV, alpha_HtuV, beta_HtuV, alphap_HtuV, Norm_Htubar, alpha_Htubar, beta_Htubar, alphap_Htqbar, Norm_HtdV, alpha_HtdV, beta_HtdV, alphap_HtdV, Norm_Htdbar, alpha_Htdbar, beta_Htdbar, Norm_Htg, alpha_Htg, beta_Htg, alphap_Htg, Norm_EtuV, alpha_EtuV, beta_EtuV, alphap_EtuV, Norm_EtdV, R_Et_Sea, R_Htu_xi2, R_Htd_xi2, R_Htg_xi2, R_Etu_xi2, R_Etd_xi2, R_Etg_xi2, R_Htu_xi4, R_Htd_xi4, R_Htg_xi4, R_Etu_xi4, R_Etd_xi4, R_Etg_xi4, bexp_HtSea, jpsinorm)[source]

Total \(\chi^2\) cost function for the GUMP global GPD fit.

Accepts all GPD model parameters as individual keyword arguments (the iMinuit interface requires a flat parameter signature). Internally the flat list is split into unpolarized (Paralst_Unp_Names), polarized (Paralst_Pol_Names), and auxiliary (Paralst_Aux_Names) groups, assembled via ParaManager_Unp() and ParaManager_Pol(), and passed to all theory prediction functions in parallel.

The returned scalar is:

\[\chi^2_\text{total} = \chi^2_\text{exp} + \chi^2_\text{PDF/GFF/GPD} + \chi^2_\text{penalty}\]

where the penalty encodes the quark-number sum rules and the momentum/gravitomagnetic sum rules with tolerances given by tolerances.

When Export_Mode is True the function prints a per-dataset \(\chi^2\) breakdown, saves results to CSV via Export_Frame_Append(), and returns a dict of result DataFrames instead of a scalar.

Parameters:

  • Norm_HuV – All GPD model parameters listed in Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

  • alpha_HuV – All GPD model parameters listed in Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

  • beta_HuV – All GPD model parameters listed in Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

  • ... – All GPD model parameters listed in Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

  • jpsinorm – All GPD model parameters listed in Paralst_Unp_Names, Paralst_Pol_Names, and Paralst_Aux_Names.

Returns:

Total \(\chi^2\) (fit mode). dict: Mapping of task name → result DataFrame (export mode).

Return type:

float

gumpgpd.Minimizer.off_forward_fit_withH_withHt(Paralst_Unp, Paralst_Pol, Paralst_Aux=[1.0], export_path='.')[source]

Run the GUMP global GPD fit using iMinuit (MIGRAD + HESSE).

Sets up a iminuit.Minuit instance with cost_off_forward_withH_withHt() as the cost function, applies parameter limits and fixes (see source for details), and calls migrad() followed by hesse(). The fit summary (timing, \(\chi^2/\text{dof}\), parameter values and uncertainties) is written to a text file under <export_path>/GUMP_Output/.

Parameters:

  • Paralst_Unp (array-like) – Initial values for all unpolarized parameters in the order defined by Paralst_Unp_Names.

  • Paralst_Pol (array-like) – Initial values for all polarized parameters in the order defined by Paralst_Pol_Names.

  • Paralst_Aux (array-like, optional) – Initial values for auxiliary parameters (currently only jpsinorm). Defaults to [1.0].

  • export_path (str, optional) – Root directory for the output text file. Defaults to the current working directory.

Returns:

The fitted Minuit object (values, errors, covariance matrix, and status flags accessible via the standard iMinuit API).

Return type:

iminuit.Minuit

Note

Export_Mode must be False when calling this function; use the cost function directly with config.Export_Mode = True to export predictions after fitting.
